html:
SMTO-SKL-0152 — That Slack reaction was already gone

GUID: a095ca77-66f7-53e4-8e77-87e81df4455c
Slug: slack-reaction-absent
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to remove a reaction that isn't on that Slack message from the Slack account SMTO uses. There was nothing to remove, so SMTO left the message as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the message in Slack and check that the reaction from SMTO's Slack account isn't showing. Slack reported that this reaction from SMTO's Slack account isn't on the message.
  2. If you meant a different emoji or a different message, ask the Agent to remove that specific emoji from that specific message. SMTO can only remove its own reactions, not ones other people added, and this one wasn't there.

What success looks like

  • The message in Slack doesn't show that reaction from SMTO's Slack account.

If it still fails

  • If the reaction from SMTO's Slack account still shows, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Slack connection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned no_reaction for reactions.remove; the service treats the reaction as absent and returns present=false, changed=false without another write.

What this means

  • Slack returns no_reaction for the selected reaction-removal request. The provider reports the desired reaction already absent, and the reaction service treats that as changed=false rather than issuing another write.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns no_reaction for the selected reaction-removal request.

How to diagnose it

  • Confirm the exact reaction request identity and provider result.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No fix is needed: SlackService.reaction maps slack.reaction_absent to a successful no-op (present=false, changed=false). If a different message or emoji was intended, issue remove_reaction with the exact channel_id, ts and name.

Retry and execution caution

  • The desired reaction is already absent; no additional write is needed.

How to verify the fix

  • The service returns present=false with changed=false.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The provider reports the desired reaction already absent, and the reaction service treats that as changed=false rather than issuing another write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
